original_question: Does every hyperkahler manifold admit a deformation that carries a Lagrangian fibration?
target_in_paper: §1.6, Question 5: "Does every hyperkähler manifold admit a deformation with a Lagrangian fibration?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual question. It correctly captures the universal quantifier (every hyperkähler manifold), the deformation-theoretic nature of the problem (existence of some deformation), and the target property that the deformed manifold itself admit a Lagrangian fibration.
missing_details: In this paper, a hyperkähler manifold means a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold: a compact, simply connected Kähler manifold whose space of holomorphic forms is generated by a nowhere-degenerate holomorphic 2-form (§1.1, p. 1).
The setting is holomorphic/complex-algebraic geometry over the complex numbers, not merely differential-geometric hyperkähler geometry (§1, especially §1.1 and §1.6).
A Lagrangian fibration is defined in §1.6 as a proper holomorphic map h:(X,σ)→B whose general fibre F is connected, has dimension half of dim X, and satisfies σ|F=0 (§1.6, pp. 5-6).

The paper asks whether there exists some member of the deformation class of X with such a fibration; it does not restrict the question to small deformations, even though small deformations are discussed nearby as evidence (§1.6, p. 7).

The intended meaning is an actual Lagrangian fibration on the deformed manifold, not merely a bimeromorphic model carrying one; Beauville explicitly distinguishes that weaker birational version in the immediately following Question 6 (§1.6, p. 7).

No extra assumptions such as projectivity, the existence of a nef isotropic line bundle, or a fixed dimension beyond the implicit notation dim X=2r are part of Question 5; those belong to the neighboring Conjecture 2 and surrounding discussion (§1.6, pp. 6-7).
refined_question: Let X be a compact hyperkähler manifold over C (equivalently, an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold). Does there exist a complex deformation X' of X and a proper surjective holomorphic map h:X'→B to a complex manifold B such that, if dim X'=2r, the general fibre F of h is connected, has dimension r, and the holomorphic symplectic form on X' restricts to 0 on F? Equivalently: does every hyperkähler deformation class contain a member admitting a holomorphic Lagrangian fibration?
justification: The draft is essentially Beauville’s Question 5 in §1.6, only lacking the paper’s ambient setup and the precise definition of a Lagrangian fibration. The surrounding context in §1.6 defines what Beauville means by a Lagrangian fibration, explains via Theorem 4 why such fibrations are the relevant nontrivial morphisms from compact hyperkähler manifolds, and places Question 5 next to Conjecture 2, which gives a line-bundle criterion for actual or birational Lagrangian fibrations. Beauville further notes that, assuming Conjecture 2, Question 5 would have a positive answer exactly when the Beauville-Bogomolov form q is indefinite. So the nearest paper-faithful target is not Conjecture 2 itself, but Question 5, with the §1.6 definition built in.
